questions.question: A person travels in a car at 40 km/h for 3 hours, on a bike at 30 km/h for 2 hours, and in a train at 80 km/h for 5 hours. What is the average speed at which he travelled?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = (40 × 3) + (30 × 2) + (80 × 5) = 120 + 60 + 400 = 580 km

Total time = 3 + 2 + 5 = 10 hours

Average Speed = 580 ÷ 10 = 58 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 58 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/141397599b86d183cd26ad70d945a313273880b9597a6d48ba123a2013d2a868.png] 

**Given:**

Car Speed = 40 km/h, Time = 3 hours

Bike Speed = 30 km/h, Time = 2 hours

Train Speed = 80 km/h, Time = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance₁ = 40 × 3 = 120 km

⇒ Distance₂ = 30 × 2 = 60 km

⇒ Distance₃ = 80 × 5 = 400 km

⇒ Total Distance = 120 + 60 + 400 = 580 km

⇒ Total Time = 3 + 2 + 5 = 10 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 580 ÷ 10 = 58 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 58 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, average speed = 2uv ÷ (u+v).

Relative Speed

For objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = s₁ − s₂. In opposite directions, relative speed = s₁ + s₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Shankar covers a certain distance by a car driving at 40 km/h and he returns to the starting point riding on a scooter with a speed of 20 km/h. Find the average speed of the whole journey.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** covered is the same for two parts of a journey, use the formula:

**Average Speed** = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 40 × 20) ÷ (40 + 20) = 1600 ÷ 60 = 80/3 km/h

Average Speed = 26 2/3 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 26 2/3 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed during onward journey (S₁) = 40 km/h

Speed during return journey (S₂) = 20 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ea4d1df9e64523c64e214f83ceb973a76fef5fc6498e874ba0e6e169af09bc4.png] 

⇒ Let the **distance** between the starting point and the turning point be **d** km.

⇒ Time taken to travel from A to B (t₁) = d ÷ 40 hours.

⇒ Time taken to travel from B back to A (t₂) = d ÷ 20 hours.

⇒ Total distance covered = d + d = **2d** km.

⇒ Total time taken = (d ÷ 40) + (d ÷ 20) = (d + 2d) ÷ 40 = **3d ÷ 40** hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 2d ÷ (3d ÷ 40)

⇒ Average Speed = (2d × 40) ÷ 3d = 80 ÷ 3 km/h.

⇒ Average Speed = 26 2/3 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 2/3 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

If distances d₁, d₂ are covered with speeds s₁, s₂, then Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) ÷ (d₁/s₁ + d₂/s₂).

Harmonic Mean Property

When distances are equal, the average speed is the **Harmonic Mean** of the individual speeds.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered with speeds x, y, and z, then Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).</p

questions.question: A man walks from point X to Y at a speed of 20 km/h, but comes back from point Y to X at a speed of 25 km/h. Find his average speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** traveled is the same (X to Y and Y to X), Average Speed = [2 × a × b] ÷ [a + b].

Average Speed = [2 × 20 × 25] ÷ [20 + 25] = 1000 ÷ 45.

Average Speed = 200 ÷ 9 = 22 2/9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 2/9 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e076f8d012a1df24c577484091d624bccb3950ff48d657f9610d3761d68ff4a.png] 

**Given:** Speed from **X to Y** (v₁) = 20 km/h, Speed from **Y to X** (v₂) = 25 km/h.

**Formula Used:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Let the distance between X and Y be the **LCM** of 20 and 25, which is 100 km.

⇒ Time taken from X to Y (t₁) = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 hours.

⇒ Time taken from Y to X (t₂) = 100 ÷ 25 = 4 hours.

⇒ Total distance = 100 + 100 = 200 km.

⇒ Total time = 5 + 4 = 9 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 200 ÷ 9 = 22 2/9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 2/9 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Time

If a person travels for **equal time intervals** at speeds v₁ and v₂, then the Average Speed = (v₁ + v₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (u + v). When in the **same direction**, it is the difference (u − v).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered at speeds a, b, and c, then Average Speed = (3 × a × b × c) ÷ (ab + bc + ca).</p

questions.question: A person covers a certain distance by bus at 45 km/h and immediately returns to the starting point by car at a speed of 80 km/h. What is his average speed during the whole journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of bus = 45 km/h

Speed of car = 80 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = frac{ { Total Distance Covered }}{ { Total Time Taken }}

**Calculation:**

Let the distance covered by person by bus be d.

When the person travels by bus the time taken can be calculated as:

Time Taken = Distance/Speed = d over 45

When the person travels by car, the distance will be same. So, time taken can be calculated as:

Time Taken = Distance/Speed = d over 80

The total time taken for the entire journey can be calculated as:

Total time taken = d over 45 + d over 80

Also, the Total Distance covered = 2d

So, Average speed can be calculated as:

⇒ (2 d)/(frac{d){45}+(d)/(80)}

⇒ (2 d)/(16 d + 9d over 720)

⇒ (2 d)/(frac{25 d){720}} 

⇒ (2 d times 720)/(25 d) 

⇒ 57.6 km/h

 ∴ **The average speed for the whole journey is 57.6 km/h.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

If distance is constant, the average speed = (2 times S₁ times S₂)/((S₁ + S₂)) [ where S1 and S2 are two speeds ]

Average speed = (2 times 45 times 80)/((45 + 80)) = 288/5 = 57.6 km/hr

questions.question: The distance between two stations, A and B, is 428 km. a train starts from station ‘A’ at 6:00 a.m and moves towards station ‘B’ at an average speed of 48 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 6:20 a.m and moves towards statin ‘A’ at an average speed of 55 km/h. At what time will the trains meet?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Train A travels alone for 20 minutes (1/3 hour) → Distance = 48 × (1/3) = 16 km.

Remaining distance at 6:20 a.m. = 428 − 16 = 412 km.

Relative speed = 48 + 55 = 103 km/h.

Time to meet = 412 ÷ 103 = 4 hours after 6:20 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:20 a.m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total Distance = 428 km, Speed of Train A = 48 km/h (starts 6:00 a.m.), Speed of Train B = 55 km/h (starts 6:20 a.m.).

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time; Relative Speed (Opposite direction) = S₁ + S₂.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/473a638769ae5dc5176fbafc6363f8f78a1ee6a893e201d9fcd66de1bb73d86c.png] 

⇒ Distance covered by Train A in 20 mins = 48 × (20/60) = 16 km.

⇒ Distance between trains at 6:20 a.m. = 428 − 16 = 412 km.

⇒ Relative speed = 48 + 55 = 103 km/h.

⇒ Time taken to meet = 412 ÷ 103 = 4 hours.

⇒ Meeting time = 6:20 a.m. + 4 hours = 10:20 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:20 a.m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move toward each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Meeting Time Rule

To calculate meeting time, ensure both objects start moving from their respective positions at the same reference time by calculating initial distance covered.

Unit Conversion

Always convert time into hours when speed is in km/h: 1 minute = 1/60 hour.</p

questions.question: A truck covers three equal distances of 100 km at the speed of 200 km/hr, 300 km/hr and 600 km/hr. Find the average speed of the truck for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For three **equal distances** covered at speeds x, y, and z, the **average speed** is the **Harmonic Mean** of the speeds.

Let the assumed distance for each segment be the **LCM** of (200, 300, 600) = 600 km.

Time taken for each segment = 600/200 = 3 h, 600/300 = 2 h, 600/600 = 1 h.

Total time = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 hours | Total distance = 3 × 600 = 1800 km.

Average speed = 1800 ÷ 6 = 300 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 300 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three equal distances d = 100 km each; Speeds v₁ = 200 km/h, v₂ = 300 km/h, v₃ = 600 km/h.

**Formula Used:** Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26b3997a8f121938dcbbe7f1662aed050982f571772e539f2f14248c0ae7707c.png] 

⇒ **Total Distance** = 100 + 100 + 100 = 300 km

⇒ Time for 1st part (t₁) = 100 ÷ 200 = 1/2 hour

⇒ Time for 2ⁿd part (t₂) = 100 ÷ 300 = 1/3 hour

⇒ Time for 3rd part (t₃) = 100 ÷ 600 = 1/6 hour

⇒ **Total Time** = (1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6) = (3 + 2 + 1) ÷ 6 = 6/6 = 1 hour

⇒ **Average Speed** = 300 ÷ 1 = 300 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 300 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distance Segments

If a distance is divided into **n equal parts** with speeds v₁, v₂, ..., vₙ, the average speed is n ÷ (1/v₁ + 1/v₂ + ... + 1/vₙ).

Two Equal Distances Case

For two **equal distances** covered at speeds x and y, the **Average Speed** is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A boy goes from home to school at a speed of 30 km/h and returns back at a speed of 70 km/h. What is his average speed for the journey?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** covered is the same for two different speeds, use the **Harmonic Mean** shortcut.

**Average Speed** = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 30 × 70) ÷ (30 + 70)

⇒ Average Speed = 4200 ÷ 100 = 42 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from **Home to School** (S₁) = 30 km/h

Speed from **School to Home** (S₂) = 70 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/053c50bf299dc039506c859d88e1dcde0ffd0f2ad9ee8e25d6078dec9024508d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance between Home and School be **210 km** (LCM of 30 and 70).

⇒ Time taken to reach school (T₁) = Distance ÷ S₁ = 210 ÷ 30 = 7 hours

⇒ Time taken to return home (T₂) = Distance ÷ S₂ = 210 ÷ 70 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 210 + 210 = 420 km

⇒ Total Time = 7 + 3 = 10 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 420 ÷ 10 = 42 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

If a person covers distances d₁, d₂, d₃ with speeds s₁, s₂, s₃, then Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (d₁/s₁ + d₂/s₂ + d₃/s₃).

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a person travels at different speeds for **equal time intervals**, the Average Speed is the **Arithmetic Mean**: (s₁ + s₂ + ... + sₙ) ÷ n.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Akhil rides first 12 km at a speed of 16 km/h and further 6 km at a speed of 20 km/h. Find his average speed (in km/h).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Total Distance** = 12 + 6 = 18 km

**Total Time** = (12 ÷ 16) + (6 ÷ 20) = 3/4 + 3/10 = (15 + 6) / 20 = 21/20 hours

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 18 ÷ (21/20) = 18 × 20 / 21 = 120 / 7 km/h

**Average Speed** = 17(1/7) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 17(1/7) km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ (d₁) = 12 km, Speed₁ (s₁) = 16 km/h

Distance₂ (d₂) = 6 km, Speed₂ (s₂) = 20 km/h

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = (Total Distance) / (Total Time)

**Time** = Distance / Speed
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7916557ef5f58ea4343cde6cfa24af3e2d9e8af91703c61f7aa82cfdc1cb2090.png] 
⇒ Time taken for first part (t₁) = 12 / 16 = 3/4 hours

⇒ Time taken for second part (t₂) = 6 / 20 = 3/10 hours

⇒ Total Time (T) = 3/4 + 3/10 = (15 + 6) / 20 = 21/20 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 18 / (21/20)

⇒ Average Speed = (18 × 20) / 21 = 360 / 21 = 120 / 7

⇒ Average Speed = 17(1/7) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 17(1/7) km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy / (x + y).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of speeds (s₁ + s₂). In the same direction, it is the difference |s₁ − s₂|.

Conversion Factor

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: If a truck moves at a constant speed of 30 km/h for 1 kilometre and 45 km/h for the next 1 kilometre. What is the average speed of the truck?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When a **truck** covers two equal distances at different speeds, the **Average Speed** is the **Harmonic Mean** of the two speeds.

Formula: Average Speed = (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂)

Calculation: (2 × 30 × 45) ÷ (30 + 45) = 2700 ÷ 75 = 36 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First speed (v₁) = 30 km/h, Distance (d₁) = 1 km

Second speed (v₂) = 45 km/h, Distance (d₂) = 1 km

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf2cc828a1611862b2c39fa5b5a51d51ba8203d77e90643be407833937ecf4fc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 1 km + 1 km = 2 km

⇒ Time taken for the first km (t₁) = Distance ÷ Speed = 1/30 hours

⇒ Time taken for the second km (t₂) = Distance ÷ Speed = 1/45 hours

⇒ Total Time = t₁ + t₂ = 1/30 + 1/45

⇒ Total Time = (3 + 2) ÷ 90 = 5/90 = 1/18 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 2 ÷ (1/18) = 2 × 18

⇒ Average Speed = 36 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 36 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Average Speed

Average speed is always calculated as the **Total Distance** divided by the **Total Time** taken for the entire journey.

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a body travels for two equal time intervals at speeds x and y, the average speed is the **Arithmetic Mean**: (x + y) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p
